input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages on Customer of 15% of annual Fees for each week an invoice is late — triggered by a minor breach and, compounding weekly, capable of exceeding the remaining contract value. That is walk-away territory and fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees). No other Customer-payable liquidated amount or termination minimum exists: Section 9.4 confirms Customer owes only accrued Fees on termination without cause, and Section 27 termination is "without penalty", so this is not a double-flag of any T4C term. We propose replacing Section 7.7 with an express no-liquidated-damages statement, which removes the formula entirely and leaves the balance of Section 7 (including the disputed-amount and no-interest mechanics in 7.3) intact.

mappings.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.

proposal.summary: Replace Customer-payable late-payment liquidated damages with an express no-liquidated-damages provision.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages payable by us, particularly 15% of annual Fees per week for a late invoice, which far exceeds any conceivable loss. We have replaced Section 7.7 with an express statement that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties; if a liquidated amount is unavoidable, our fallback is an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole such amount.
